whatThePageStates: A short how-to page about running AWS Verified Access in a FIPS 140-2 compliant configuration. Its one and only coverage statement is a single introductory bullet list: "FIPS compliance for Verified Access is available in the following AWS Regions", followed by seven region names. The remainder of the page is procedural — two numbered walkthroughs, one for converting an existing Verified Access environment (delete and re-create endpoints, groups and instance) and one for building a new FIPS-enabled environment (trust provider, instance with FIPS turned on, group, endpoints). There is no table, no matrix, no Yes/No column, and no statement anywhere that FIPS is unavailable in any named Region.

features.statuses: 7 supported (available), 0 not-supported, 0 partial; 7+0+0=7. The page uses a bare inclusion list introduced by 'available in the following AWS Regions', so every listed value reads as a Yes. Not-supported is ABSENT, not stated: no Region is named and denied, and there is no 'not available in' or exclusion note. Any count of unsupported Regions would have to be derived from an external Region list, which this page does not provide.
features.scope: None. The availability list is flat — it is not qualified by instance type, endpoint type, trust-provider type, plan, or console-versus-API. The two procedures below apply everywhere FIPS is available and do not subdivide the list. The only latent second dimension is partition: five of the seven values are commercial (aws) Regions and two are GovCloud (aws-us-gov), but the page presents them in one undifferentiated list and makes no partition-level claim.
features.reasoning: The enumerated values are AWS Region names — a universe that exists independently of Verified Access — so the axis is region and the kind is external. The unit of claim is one Region per bullet: each bullet asserts that the FIPS-compliant configuration of Verified Access can be used in that Region. Rows do not collapse — each of the seven bullets names a different Region, so expectedCount equals distinct targets and the extra fields are omitted.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' list (two in-page anchors: Existing environment, New environment) is navigation, not coverage. The two H2 procedure sections and their numbered steps are instructions, not claims — the four steps under each are workflow items, not axis values, and the linked page names (trust provider, user identity, device-based, instance, group, endpoints) are cross-references, not supported-thing enumerations. The bolded UI label 'Federal Information Process Standards (FIPS)' is a console control. The definitional sentence about FIPS being a US and Canadian government standard is background. The whole 'See also' block — the AWS agent-toolkit skills boilerplate and its CLI command and link — is stock footer text present on many pages and carries no coverage.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this is the only dimension the page supplies — seven named Regions where FIPS compliance for Verified Access is available (US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), AWS GovCloud (US) West, AWS GovCloud (US) East). It gives an inclusion list only; it never enumerates or counts Regions where the feature is absent, so no unsupported-Region figure can be taken from this page. SERVICE: nothing. The page is about exactly one service, AWS Verified Access; it does not compare or enumerate services, and 'seven' is a Region count, not a service count. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. Verified Access instances, groups, endpoints and trust providers appear as procedure steps in a setup walkthrough, not as a list of resource types that do or do not support FIPS — the page never says any of them is unsupported, so treating those four nouns as a covered/uncovered axis fabricates a claim the page does not make.
trap: The single most likely misparse is harvesting the two numbered procedures as coverage: each walkthrough has four steps naming Verified Access resources (instance, group, endpoint, trust provider), which a careless parser reads as a resourceType axis of four supported items — or, worse, sums them with the seven Regions to report eleven or fifteen 'supported' values. Runners-up: (1) inferring unsupported Regions by differencing the seven against the full AWS Region list and reporting a No count the page never states; (2) counting the two 'Topics' anchors, or the two H2 sections, as two configuration modes that are 'supported'; (3) reading 'US and Canadian government standard' and pulling US and Canada as a country axis; (4) scraping the 'See also' agent-toolkit paragraph as feature availability; (5) silently merging the two GovCloud entries with the five commercial Regions when the consumer wants a partition-scoped answer, or conversely double-counting them as both regions and a partition claim.
